messages:
maria: Heads up — Ubuntu base images built yesterday pulled in upstream glibc patch for CVE-2026-2107 and OpenSSL 1.1.1n with fixes. I ran a quick vuln scan and we still show high sev findings on arm64 variants. Do we treat this as a critical rebuild or schedule during our next maintenance window?

alex: Can you paste the scan output? Need CVSS and whether there are known exploits. If it's only distros with backports and no public exploit, we might do staged canary.

maria: Paste excerpt:
```
Package: libc6 (glibc)
Version: 2.31-0ubuntu9.24
CVE: CVE-2026-2107 CVSS: 9.1
Note: local privilege escalation reported, limited PoC on linux-4.x kernels (public PoC but requires specific kernel config)
---
openssl 1.1.1n-1ubuntu2.3 CVE-2026-1173 CVSS: 7.8 - remote side-channel vector, no known RCE
```

sam: If there's a PoC for local privilege escalation, we should prioritise images that run untrusted code (build agents, CI runners, sandboxed user tasks). For other infra (internal controllers) we can schedule. Which images carry the vulnerable libc? user-facing runtime images?

maria: Affected lists: runtime/generic:latest (amd64/arm64), ci/runners:stable-arm64, base/alpine layers are fine (no glibc). Runtime is the priority.

jordan: Proposed plan:
- Emergency rebuild of runtime/generic for both amd64 and arm64 with pinned repros (digest bump)
- Run smoke + security e2e on canary cluster (1 node per region)
- 24h observation, then rollout to staged fleet (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
- If errors, automatic rollback to previous digest

priya: Quick Q: any KMS/key rotation impact for image signing? We sign images after CI. If we need a rollback, we should keep previous signed digests available.

alex: CI can rebuild and sign automatically. We need to ensure our signing key in KMS is available in all regions used for canary. Also add an audit log entry for the rebuild job: WHY=security-fix, CVEs, trigger=user:maria.

deploy-bot: ci-image-rebuild triggered by @maria for runtime/generic:latest - build 2026-03-20T14:08Z - sha256:old -> sha256:new. Status: queued.

maria: Tests to run on canary:
- startup-time smoke
- tokenized inference latency (p50/p95)
- KV-cache correctness (sanity prompts)
- container privilege verification (no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, seccomp enabled)
- audit logging: confirm new image emits container start/stop events to audit-logs S3 bucket

sam: Add quick grep for setuid binaries in the image "find / -perm -4000 -type f" and fail the build if found. Also validate glibc version with `ldd --version`.

maria: Agree. Also, for the arm64 variant we need a cross-compile check — historical flakes on aarch64 kernel configs. Add an explicit kernel smoke: run minimal syscall fuzz for 10s in canary.

jordan: Rollout timing: we should avoid pushing to Dedicated customer hosts during daytime SLAs. Suggested schedule: start canary now, hold full rollout to Dedicated until 02:00 PT maintenance window. Hosted API can go faster (we can route 5% traffic to canary).

priya: Customer comms? For Dedicated customers we'll send a heads-up email about a security rebuild and potential short maintenance window. For Hosted, mention we are rolling security rebuilds with no expected downtime.

alex: Ops checklist for rebuild job:
1) update base Dockerfile to Ubuntu:20.04 + apt update/upgrade
2) set APT::Immediate-Configure to true in build to ensure clean deps (inline config)
3) pin package digest via apt-get download and create reproducible layer
4) sign image with KMS key: projects/redwood/kms/image-signing-key
5) push to canary registry with tag runtime/generic:2026-03-20-secfix

maria: One concern: older models pinned to older runtimes might break if libc ABI changes. We must test model-serving containers pinned to previous images and ensure compatibility. If incompatible, we need a compatibility shim or keep old image available for those customers.

sam: Let's capture compatibility tests in CI matrix: run a sample of pinned-models (top 10 by usage) against the new image. If any fail, escalate to eng-runtime for quick investigation.

jordan: Rollback plan: if canary fails, deploy-bot will automatically revert route and pull previous digest. Manual escalation path: page oncall@redwood with severity-high.

maria: Action items I will do now: trigger rebuild (started), add grep for suid, add glibc version gate, add aarch64 syscall-smoke. Alex — can you validate KMS signing availability in eu-west1 and us-west1? Sam — add pinned-model compatibility suite into the job. Jordan — prepare canary cluster and rollout policy. Priya — draft customer comms.

priya: I'll draft a 1-paragraph note for Dedicated customers + short hosted banner. Will share in #announcements for review. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: ci-image-rebuild build 2026-03-20T14:21Z - sha256:new started, tests queued.

maria: Thanks team. Keep updates here. If anything high-sev shows up in canary, tag with :rotating_light: and escalate.

alex: Noted. Also let's add an audit log event to mark this triage decision: security:accepted-risk=false, priority=high, rationale=public PoC for LPE.

sam: One last note — alpine-based images are unaffected but double-check musl-linked tooling we use in tests.

maria: Good call. I'll include a musl smoke to ensure we didn't regress any cross-image behavior.

jordan: Will monitor canary and post results in ~30m.

maria: (added) test results: canary passed smoke + security e2e, no regressions detected. Starting staged rollout to 10%.

jordan: Noticed slight p95 latency bump (+3%) on region us-west1, likely kernel scheduler warmup. Observing.

sam: If p95 >5% for >60m, auto-rollback.

maria: OK. Leaving this thread open for final confirmation.
